headline: 12-year-old girl swept away by floodwaters in Cox’s Bazar
summary: The child died after falling from a boat while crossing floodwaters in Chakaria; her two sisters were rescued in critical condition.
details: A 12-year-old girl, identified as Hasnatul Jannat Jharna, died after being swept away by floodwaters in Cox’s Bazar’s Chakaria upazila today.
The incident occurred around 11:20 am in the Rasulabad area when Jharna and her two sisters were crossing the water by boat. All three fell into the water and went missing.
Fire Service and Civil Defence personnel launched a rescue operation, recovering Jharna's body at approximately 1:50 pm.
Her two sisters, Sawrin Moni and Jerin, were rescued in critical condition and are currently undergoing treatment in a hospital.
Heavy rainfall and hill runoff have severely disrupted life across Cox’s Bazar, with at least 150 villages in 35 unions across 10 upazilas flooded.
More than 300,000 people have been left stranded as floodwaters submerged hundreds of homes, schools, and rural roads.
The worst-hit areas include Chakaria, Pekua, and Matamuhuri, while other regions like Cox’s Bazar Sadar, Ukhiya, and Teknaf are also affected.
The Cox’s Bazar Meteorological Office recorded 71 mm of rainfall in the district within 24 hours leading up to 3:00 pm today.

summary: The Jamaat-e-Islami ameer has emphasized the duty to support those impacted by floods, leading relief distribution efforts in affected areas.
details: The Jamaat-e-Islami ameer has stated that it is a humanitarian responsibility to stand by people affected by floods. He emphasized that supporting those in distress is a moral obligation that transcends political affiliations.

The Jamaat-e-Islami ameer has stated that it is a humanitarian responsibility to stand by people affected by floods. He emphasized that supporting those in distress is a moral obligation that transcends political affiliations.
